commit_message:
[gxvar] Reduce number of mallocs.

8% speed up in drawing GoogleSansFlex variable in HB benchmark-font.

* src/truetype/ttgxvar.c (TT_Vary_Apply_Glyph_Deltas): Use an allocation
  pool instead of individual allocations.

fix_commit_message:
* src/truetype/ttgxvar.c (TT_Vary_Apply_Glyph_Deltas): Fix allocation.

Bug was introduced in commit 582de1a4b6f.
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 702e4a1d32e4 on top of intro 582de1a4b6f6 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (BufferOverflow): FreeType's TrueType GX variable font support (ttgxvar.c, TT_Vary_Apply_Glyph_Deltas) was refactored in commit 582de1a4b to replace five individual heap allocations with one combined pool allocation sized as the sum of per-field byte sizes. Four of the five size computations correctly multiply the element count by the element's sizeof, but the computation for peak_coords_size forgot the sizeof(FT_Fixed) multiplier, reserving only 3*num_axis bytes instead of 3*num_axis*sizeof(FT_Fixed) bytes for an FT_Fixed array. Because peak_coords is the first sub-buffer in the pool and subsequent sub-buffers are placed immediately after it by pointer arithmetic, writes to peak_coords (and the derived im_start_coords/im_end_coords pointers) beyond the undersized region corrupt adjacent pool contents and can write out of bounds of the overall heap allocation when processing a malicious variable font's `gvar` table with a sufficient number of axes/points. Root cause: Inconsistent/incomplete arithmetic when converting an array-element-count-based allocation macro (FT_QNEW_ARRAY, which handles sizeof internally) into a manual pool-size computation; the sizeof multiplier for one of five sub-buffers (peak_coords, an FT_Fixed array) was dropped while it was correctly applied to the other four, so the pool undersizes the first field by a factor of sizeof(FT_Fixed).
